_note: Project switches (v2.48.0; v2.49.0 adds frame-led, guide-audio, floor-1080 and dwg-working; 2026-11-03: "I think such choices are project based?" then "yes"). A house rule stays the default for every job. A job turns ONE named rule off by writing the switch in its 00-brief/CHECKPOINT.md `Switches:` line with a reason (`<id> — <reason>; <id> — <reason>`, or `none`). gate.py open validates the line against this file; scripts/switches.py reads it; every script that enforces a lifted rule prints the rule as lifted, with the reason, instead of refusing. A switch lifts only what its `lifts` says. Anything in `locked` is never a switch.

music-led.lifts: Music to picture: 'fit the track to the cut, never the cut to the track'. The song is fixed and is the deliverable; the picture is cut to it.
music-led.allows: cutting picture to the song's beats and sections; the song's own sections setting the camera's energy; a move, freeze or burst cued to a sound in the song (the burst still counts against the ramp cap).
music-led.still_holds: a genre-to-camera mapping (cinematography-craft.md §3.9) stays out; never picking music autonomously (the song is the client's).

speed-conform.lifts: The ramp rules (titles-and-motion C4: the cap and `reveal=`) for two declared cases: a whole-clip constant conform on the shot (a real high-frame-rate shot played slower across the whole clip, or a lip-sync take shot off-speed and conformed), and a shallow ease inside a planned whip (100 % down to no less than 85 % and back).
speed-conform.allows: `conform=<speed>%` on a shot (or `conform=<src fps>/<timeline fps>`), and `ease=<min speed>%` (85 or more) on a shot that carries `join: whip`; neither counts as a ramp or needs `reveal=`.
speed-conform.still_holds: the frame-repeat floor (timeline fps / source fps); any other speed change inside a clip is still a ramp; a burst that hides a mask join stays out with the mask wipe (locked: no roto).

upload-master.lifts: Delivering at the format's resolution and no higher (realism-qa V15, the UGC lane) for one extra upload copy: a master of the same shape at a larger size (e.g. 2160p from a 1080 delivery).
upload-master.allows: export_qc.py --upload-master on that copy: the same shape as the preset, a larger size, every other check unchanged.
upload-master.still_holds: the delivered file itself still matches its preset exactly.

finish-texture.lifts: grade-finish C2: ads get no texture node, no bloom, no grain and no vignette.
finish-texture.allows: a small bloom, optional grain and a light vignette in the ads lane's grade plan.
finish-texture.still_holds: skin protection; look strength; look_qa export.
finish-texture.when: A look that already reads as film (lifestyle, beauty, nostalgic, period, music-video): a small bloom, halation only on an explicitly filmic brief; grain to unify mixed sources or dither banding; the motivated vignette window where the edges compete with the subject.
finish-texture.not_when: Clean tech, SaaS, fintech, explainer or high-key looks; product-clarity shots, packshots, UI and text-heavy frames; clipped highlights; heavy grain on a hero product; grain the brief needs seen on Reels or TikTok.
finish-texture.where: Bloom, then halation, then grain on the clip's texture node in the 9:16 timeline (people and b-roll; product, anatomy and clean shots stay clean), never the Timeline graph; the window static on a clip node; the lens vignette centred on the safe box, not the frame.
finish-texture.how_much: No portable slider numbers. One small bloom; grain from C2's 3–6 %, one setting on every textured shot, out if the round trip strips it; vignette by eye, no ring, the subject's level healthy.
finish-texture.guide: references/editing-and-audio.md § Finishing looks (bloom, glow and halation; film grain; vignette)
rule_refs: references/editing-and-audio.md § The grade (the template and step 3)

light-leak.lifts: The ban on flares, glows and leaks in ads and launches (product-video.md §2.5).
light-leak.allows: one light-leak hit on one cut, screen-blended and peaking on the transition, inside the accent budget (titles-and-motion C5).
light-leak.still_holds: never as a grade, never on every cut; the C5 budget.
light-leak.when: Motivated by film or a real light source: a roll's head or tail, a Super 8 or nostalgic register, memory or flashback, a music-video flash that says something.
light-leak.not_when: A generic pack transition or a cover for a weak cut; unmotivated stock on digital footage; a TikTok ad meant to look native; saturated leaks over faces.
light-leak.where: One hit on one cut the brief already motivates, peaking on the cut; an Edit-page transition or a Screen overlay, never a grade node; captions, titles, the product and the disclosure stay clear of it.
light-leak.how_much: No reliable count or opacity (the course tries 50 down to 20 on Screen); at most 3 flashes a second over a quarter of the screen (Ofcom, WCAG 2.3.1); desaturate before it reaches red.

blur-titles.lifts: The ads lane's 'opacity or rise only, no blur' (typography-and-captions.md §6c item 3; title_card.py lint 'blur in ads').
blur-titles.allows: a brand line, a closing lockup or a small mark (never the hook card) entering with a blur that clears to sharp while it fades up and rises, mirrored out.
blur-titles.still_holds: native Resolve titles (titles-and-motion C7); the lane's durations and curves.
blur-titles.when: A calm, premium single line: a brand line, a logo lockup or a closing statement, once per film; a narrative or music-video title card.
blur-titles.not_when: The hook card; prices, offers, legal lines, disclosures, CTAs or captions; busy or moving backgrounds; stacked with stagger, wipe or glow.
blur-titles.where: A hero-line or lockup kind used as a brand line or closing lockup, never the hook; built native (fusion_titles.py blur-resolve, or Text+ Softness); sharp and still inside the safe box for its reading time.
blur-titles.how_much: No reliable video number: web-UI sources put the reveal at about 0.5–0.8 s; the blur clears inside the lane's entrance, and the reading floor counts from sharp.
blur-titles.guide: references/typography-and-captions.md §6c, the blur-in block after item 3 (decision rule: references/editing-and-audio.md § Finishing looks)

blurred-fill.lifts: Never an image over a blurred, stretched copy of itself (typography-and-captions.md §6c item 10).
blurred-fill.allows: a too-tight shot filling a vertical frame over a blurred, enlarged copy of the same clip, for a shot on screen about two seconds.
blurred-fill.still_holds: swapping the clip is still the first answer.
blurred-fill.when: The last resort for one too-tight vertical shot, after another shot, a reframe or Smart Reframe, a split screen and a designed or brand-colour plate, where a crop would destroy information.
blurred-fill.not_when: A paid 9:16 placement where a native version is possible; a single centred subject; a face or product that ghosts in the fill; a timeline-wide default.
blurred-fill.where: One shot, on screen about two seconds; Resolve FX Blanking Fill on the clip; on 9:16 the 16:9 band is y 656–1264, so type sits on the band or above it, never on the fill.
blurred-fill.how_much: Blurred until no shape reads, darkened slightly; no source gives a hold time, and about two seconds is this plugin's own limit.
blurred-fill.guide: references/typography-and-captions.md §6c, the blurred-fill block after item 10 (decision rule: references/editing-and-audio.md § Finishing looks)

caption-display-face.lifts: 'A display face is for a title, never for a caption run' (typography-and-captions.md §2).
caption-display-face.allows: the client's own display face for captions; a regular weight is flagged as a contrast risk rather than swapped.
caption-display-face.still_holds: title_qa's contrast check and the phone proof.

caption-shadow-first.lifts: Caption contrast in the order plate first, shadow second (typography-and-captions.md §4).
caption-shadow-first.allows: an enlarged, softened drop shadow first, and a faint dark gradient behind the type only where it still sinks.
caption-shadow-first.still_holds: the contrast gate measures the result; in the ads lane the gradient is a vignette, so it also needs finish-texture.

lens-smear.lifts: P11 (the foreground wipe, motion-craft.md §7b) for one in-camera case: a smear passed across the lens on a real shoot, used as a join outside the ads lane.
lens-smear.allows: that join, cut inside the smear.
lens-smear.still_holds: no mask drawn to follow anything (no roto); not in the ads lane.

step-lower-thirds.lifts: The deferred explainer step chips (modes/editorial-explainer.md, waiting on Q2) for one form: a lower third on the shot each step or tip names.
step-lower-thirds.allows: a native Text+ lower third per step, with no leader line.
step-lower-thirds.still_holds: leader lines wait on Q2; card words that did not read stay unread.

frame-led.lifts: The 2.49 default that a Seedance 2.5 / Cinema Studio clip is written as `form: scene` from approved reference sheets (prompting-craft.md §12).
frame-led.allows: the pre-2.49 route for this job: every clip is i2v from an approved start frame (frame:<SHOT>), clip prompts carry motion only, and CLIP_FORBIDDEN applies.
frame-led.still_holds: every other gate: sheets approved, the voice gate, the contact sheet, the quality floor.
frame-led.when: An exact composition the client approved as a still (a packshot, a logo end card, a brand composite), a product whose label must match a photograph, a series whose frames are already approved.
frame-led.not_when: To save credits, or because writing the long template feels slow.
frame-led.where: The whole job (prompt_lint.py refuses `form: scene` while it is on; gate.py requires frame:<SHOT> on every clip).

guide-audio.lifts: The 2.49 default that a clip's native diegetic sound is kept as production sound (editing-and-audio.md §7d).
guide-audio.allows: the pre-2.49 rule for this job: native sound is a timing guide only; `generate_audio: true` needs `audio` approved; mix_qa.py refuses a non-dialogue take's own sound in the export without a `native` approval.
guide-audio.still_holds: the voice gate for speech; one ambience bed per location (§7e).
guide-audio.when: A job whose sound is designed from licensed libraries end to end (a sound-designed spot), a client who asked for clean stems, a format where the model's sound is known to be poor.
guide-audio.not_when: As a habit: the festival winners kept their native sound and the judges named sound in two of three awards.

floor-1080.lifts: The 2.49 video floor of 720p (one upscale on the final, after the cut).
floor-1080.allows: nothing looser — it RESTORES the 1080p video floor for this job: prompt_lint.py and gate.py refuse a video take under 1080p.
floor-1080.when: A client who wants native 1080p or better, a hero film, close faces and wide plates throughout, a delivery above 1080p where an upscale is not acceptable.

dwg-working.lifts: editing-and-audio.md Colour management item 1's Rec.709 (Scene) working route, for REAL log footage only.
dwg-working.allows: grading real log footage in DaVinci Wide Gamut as a pair of transforms: each camera's input transform first on its own colour group's pre-clip graph (camera log and gamut to DaVinci Wide Gamut / DaVinci Intermediate, no tone or gamut mapping), then the match, look and texture, then an output transform to Rec.709 Gamma 2.4 last with tone mapping on.
dwg-working.still_holds: generated clips stay on item 1's Rec.709 route; a look LUT built on display-referred pixels goes AFTER the output transform (or the look is built by hand); the export gate (look_qa.py export); grade-finish C1–C4.
dwg-working.when: A job with real log camera footage (Canon Log, S-Log, LogC, V-Log …) graded in Resolve.
dwg-working.not_when: Generated footage, or a hybrid cut mixing generated clips into the wide space (untested).
dwg-working.where: The grade: the per-camera colour group's pre-clip graph and the timeline's last node.
dwg-working.how_much: No template until a real log job needs one.

locked.name: advanced VFX
locked.rule: Owner standing rule: no advanced VFX — mask-wipe and luma-key joins and heavy compositing stay out. Since 2.49 (2026-11-05) roto IS allowed for one job: masked-region repair with a tracked box or SAM 2 (scripts/region_repair.py), blended back as a Fusion comp in Resolve built by computer control, never through the API (2026-11-05; the tool's own composite is a preview only), so only the masked region changes.

locked.name: AI images as references
locked.rule: Owner standing rule: never use AI images as references.

locked.name: spend without approval
locked.rule: Owner standing rule: spend nothing without approval; paid generation goes through gate.py.

locked.name: non-native titles
locked.rule: Owner standing rule: always native Resolve titles (titles-and-motion C7).

locked.name: skipping the contact sheet
locked.rule: Owner standing rule: a contact sheet before any video draft.

locked.name: picking music autonomously
locked.rule: Owner standing rule: never pick music autonomously.
